name: Combined Immunodeficiency due to IKBKB Gain-of-Function Mutation

criteria.description: Identification of heterozygous gain-of-function mutation in IKBKB gene by molecular genetic testing
Clinical presentation with recurrent severe infections involving bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens
Laboratory evidence of combined immunodeficiency including abnormal T and B cell subsets and impaired lymphocyte proliferation
Elevated serum inflammatory cytokines or markers consistent with immune dysregulation
Family history of early-onset immunodeficiency or related immune dysregulation syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic IKBKB gain-of-function mutation plus clinical combined immunodeficiency phenotype with supportive immunophenotyping abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, clinical, and immunological data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe recurrent bacterial and viral infections
pathognomonic.notes: Often life-threatening infections in early infancy
searchTerms: frequent serious bacterial and viral infections
repeated infections from bacteria and viruses

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

pathognomonic.notes: Marked reduction in circulating lymphocytes and functional defects
searchTerms: low lymphocyte count with poor T cell function
immune cell deficiency with impaired T cells
reduced T cell activity and numbers

common.notes: Poor growth and weight gain in infancy
Enlargement of liver and spleen due to immune dysregulation
Due to infections or immune-mediated enteropathy

occasional.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to immune activation

rare.notes: Secondary to infections or immune-mediated damage
Chronic lung damage from recurrent infections
Autoimmune thyroid disease reported in some cases

laboratory: Lymphopenia with decreased CD4+ and CD8+ T cells
imaging: Chest radiographs showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
other: Histopathology of skin or lymphoid tissue showing immune dysregulation

distinguishingFeatures: Profound T and B cell deficiency with absent thymic shadow
Early onset with failure to thrive and opportunistic infections
Mutations in FAS pathway genes rather than IKBKB

redFlags: Severe, recurrent, and unusual infections in early infancy
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
Family history of early infant deaths or immunodeficiency
references: Kuehn HS et al. Gain-of-function IKBKB mutations cause combined immunodeficiency. J Clin Invest. 2019.
Orphanet: Combined immunodeficiency due to IKBKB gain-of-function mutation. ORPHA:700205.
